subject: Archaeology
title: Drones in Archaeology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Drones in Archaeology.

hook.text: A cheap drone can do in 20 minutes what once took a week with tapes and surveying gear.

buildup.text: Drones photograph sites from above, creating 3D models of entire excavation areas.

discovery.text: Thermal drones detect buried walls at night. Stone holds heat differently from soil.

twist.text: In conflict zones, drones monitor looting at sites too dangerous for people to visit.

climax.text: Drone photogrammetry is now standard on most digs. Aerial archaeology is democratized.

punchline.text: What once needed a helicopter now fits in a backpack.

quiz.question: How do thermal drones help archaeologists?
options: They melt ice covering frozen archaeological sites
They detect buried walls at night because stone retains heat differently
They measure excavation depth using laser scanning

details.summary: Drones equipped with cameras and sensors survey archaeological landscapes faster and cheaper than manned aircraft. They create high-resolution orthophotographs, 3D terrain models, and thermal maps that reveal buried features invisible at ground level — from field walls to entire hidden settlements.
details.whyItMatters: Drone technology has made aerial survey affordable for even small archaeological projects. Features that once required expensive helicopter flights can now be documented in hours with a consumer drone and photogrammetry software.
takeaways: Drones create centimeter-accurate 3D models of archaeological sites
Thermal cameras on drones detect buried walls and structures
Affordable technology brings aerial survey to small projects

faq.question: How do drones detect buried archaeological features?
faq.answer: Multispectral and thermal cameras detect soil moisture and temperature differences caused by buried walls, ditches, and floors. Stone walls retain heat differently than surrounding soil. Vegetation growing over buried features shows subtle color and height differences captured from above.

faq.question: What advantages do drones have over traditional aerial photography?
faq.answer: Drones fly lower, producing much higher resolution imagery. They can be deployed on demand to capture specific conditions — after rain, during crop growth, or at optimal sun angles. They cost a fraction of manned aircraft and require no runway or pilot.
